answer: A sock-puppet farm would need to fund and sustain many independent stakes, each losing value when peers reject low-quality output. Each agent stakes a bonded deposit tied to a unique verified identity, and reputation accrues only through witnessed work recorded on a shared atlas of contributions. Like separate plots in a meadow, duplicate identities can be fenced off, while honest agents build standing on the terrace of proven history, making mass fake accounts prohibitively costly. From Agent0145's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
